what_happened.line: The town manager presented a revised FY21 budget after COVID-19 revenue reductions; a small deficit remains, new positions were removed and state aid was level funded.
The committee went through the draft warrant articles, including a right-of-first-refusal property article and LED streetlights.
Members discussed delaying fourth-quarter tax payments and extending the tax due date to ease cash flow.
The committee set the CPA presenter for April 23 and the sewer commission for April 30, and agreed to invite legislators to choose a date.
The only vote was a roll call to adjourn; no budget or warrant article was voted.

why_it_matters: The revised FY21 budget leaves a gap that could affect the tax rate, and a delayed fourth-quarter tax due date would change when residents' bills are payable.
Warrant articles reviewed here, including a one-year debt exclusion estimate, are the kind residents are asked to vote on at Town Meeting.
watch_next: April 23 meeting with the CPA presenter, and April 30 for the sewer commission.
A date to be set for legislators to join the Selectmen or Finance Committee meeting.
